result:
A race condition is when two processes touch the same resource at the same time and the result depends on which one happens to run first, so the output is occasionally wrong in ways that are hard to reproduce. With a shared log, the usual symptom is interleaved or garbled lines when two scripts write at once.

Take a lock around the write with `flock`:

```sh
{
  flock 9
  echo "$(date -Is) $$ started job" >> /var/log/shared.log
} 9>/var/log/shared.log.lock
```

Every writer must use the same lock file, and the lock is released automatically when the block exits, even if the script dies.

A single short `echo ... >> file` is already safe on a local filesystem, because `>>` opens in append mode and each small write lands whole. You need the lock when one entry spans several commands or lines, or is large.

`flock` is unreliable on NFS, so there, have each host write its own file instead.
